summary: This short program asks the reader to type their name, then greets them by name. It shows how to collect input from a person and place it inside a message.

lines.text: The input function displays the prompt text, waits for the user to type something and press Enter, and hands back whatever was typed as a string, which is stored in the variable name.
The f before the quotes makes this an f-string, so Python replaces {name} with the value the user entered instead of printing the word "name" literally.
